caption:
A Matter of Fit

Why do we wear makeup?
And how much is enough?

The women who come to my sessions
are mostly in their forties and fifties —
in Japan, Singapore and Sydney alike.
I always ask what brought them.
Many have never been taught.
In their twenties, makeup felt unnecessary.
Now, they find themselves reaching for it.

For some, it is the first signs of time on the skin.
For others, it is the wardrobe —
fabrics and cuts that have quietly grown finer,
beside a bare face that no longer quite keeps up.
And for many, it is a wish for a grace
that belongs to this age.

None of them want heavy makeup.
What I offer is the Japanese way —
delicate, quietly natural,
shaped around each woman's life and mood.
This is my work, every day.

Makeup is not meant to change your face.
It is what lets your face
belong to the rest of you.
